test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Sept 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The salaries of P and Q together amount to Rs. 6,40,000. P and Q save 60% and 40%, respectively, of their individual salaries. If their expenditures are the same, then what is the ratio of P's salary to Q's salary?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Expenditure %** of P = 100% − 60% = 40%

**Expenditure %** of Q = 100% − 40% = 60%

Given: Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

⇒ 40% of **Salary P** = 60% of **Salary Q**

⇒ Salary P / Salary Q = 60 / 40 = 3 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Salary (P + Q) = ₹6,40,000

Savings of P = 60% | Savings of Q = 40%

Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78d9403b3de26ed6ac7a294c5d3c6f49e4392c73167a2d504314b0212260c999.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P be the salary of P and Q be the salary of Q.

⇒ Expenditure of P = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 60% = 40% of P

⇒ Expenditure of Q = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 40% = 60% of Q

⇒ According to the question: 40% × P = 60% × Q

⇒ (40/100) × P = (60/100) × Q

⇒ 40 × P = 60 × Q

⇒ P / Q = 60 / 40

⇒ P / Q = 3 / 2

⇒ **Ratio** = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income Formula

Total Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings: **Income = Expenditure + Savings**.

Percentage Expenditure

If a person saves x% of their income, then their expenditure percentage is **(100 − x)%** of the total income.

Ratio of Quantities

When a% of A equals b% of B, the ratio A : B is always the inverse of the percentage coefficients: **A : B = b : a**.
